counterfactual_missing_items: endoscopic confirmation of a vascular lesion
decisive_items: hematemesis; the vomitus resembled coffee grounds
contrast-enhanced CT showed no active bleeding
nasogastric tube aspirated a small amount of blood
response.rationale: R4 best explains severe persistent upper GI bleeding with negative CT, negative H. pylori, normal coagulation, and poor response to acid suppression; a vascular anomaly can be occult on CT and requires endoscopy. R5 and R6 rely on generic bleeding spans and are weakened by negative H. pylori (R6) and lack of a specific mechanism; R1 and R2 lack portal hypertension or retching history.

rejected.why: Only hematemesis is cited; no portal hypertension, liver disease, splenomegaly, or abnormal ultrasound/LFTs to support varices.
No preceding retching or vomiting; coffee-ground vomitus suggests a gastric rather than esophageal tear, and age is atypical.
H. pylori is explicitly excluded and there is no NSAID exposure; normal gastrin and lack of response to famotidine make peptic ulcer less likely.
